facts.statement: Camposaurus lived during the early to middle Norian stage of the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: The pertinent fossil remains date back to the early to middle Norian stage

facts.statement: Camposaurus was a small, carnivorous theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Camposaurus is a small, carnivorous, theropod dinosaur

facts.statement: Camposaurus has been estimated to reach a length of 3 meters.
facts.quote: Camposaurus has been estimated at 3 m in length

facts.statement: Like other coelophysids, Camposaurus possessed fused tibio-tarsals and fibulo-tarsals.
facts.quote: Like other coelophysids, it has fused tibio-tarsals and fibulo-tarsals

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives, Camposaurus had a distinct ridge at the back of the tibia where it fits with the fibula.
facts.quote: Unlike its relatives, the area of the tibia that fits with the fibula has a distinct ridge at the back

facts.statement: The type species Camposaurus arizonensis was formally named and described in 1998 by Adrian Hunt, Spencer G. Lucas, Andrew B. Heckert, Robert M. Sullivan, and Martin Lockley.
facts.quote: The type species, C. arizonensis, was formally named and described by Adrian Hunt, Spencer G. Lucas, Andrew B. Heckert, Robert M. Sullivan and Martin Lockley in 1998

facts.statement: The genus name Camposaurus means "Camp's lizard" and honors Charles Lewis Camp.
facts.quote: The genus name means "Camp's lizard", after Charles Lewis Camp

facts.statement: The species name arizonensis refers to the fact that the dinosaur was found in Arizona, United States.
facts.quote: The species name refers to the fact it was found in Arizona, in the United States

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UCMP 34498 was discovered in 1934 in the Placerias quarry of the Bluewater Creek Formation in Arizona.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen UCMP 34498 was discovered in the Placerias quarry of the Bluewater Creek Formation of Arizona, from the Norian stage of the Late Triassic period in 1934

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was not named until 1998 by Hunt and colleagues.
facts.quote: It wasn't named until 1998 by Hunt and colleagues

facts.statement: In 2000, Downs examined Camposaurus and concluded it was a junior synonym of Coelophysis.
facts.quote: In 2000, Downs examined Camposaurus and concluded that it is a junior synonym of Coelophysis

facts.statement: A 2007 review by Nesbitt et al. found that the ventral astragalar margin of Camposaurus was straight and indistinguishable from that of Coelophysis bauri.
facts.quote: The review by Nesbitt et al. in 2007, revealed that a specific feature of the ankle (the ventral astragalar margin) was found to be straight, and is indistinguishable from that of Coelophysis bauri

facts.statement: A 2011 phylogenetic analysis found Camposaurus to be a close relative of Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis.
facts.quote: In 2011, it was entered into a phylogenetic analysis and found to be a close relative of Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis

facts.statement: Many paleontologists have rejected Camposaurus as a nomen dubium due to the lack of material.
facts.quote: The lack of material has led many paleontologists to reject it as a nomen dubium

facts.statement: A reassessment by Ezcurra and Brusatte revealed two autapomorphies in the holotype, firmly establishing Camposaurus as a valid genus and species.
facts.quote: A reassessment of the holotype UCMP 34498 of Camposaurus arizoniensis by Ezcurra and Brusatte revealed two autapomorphies, thereby firmly establishing this material as a valid genus and species

facts.statement: Analysis demonstrated that Camposaurus is definitely a neotheropod.
facts.quote: This analysis also demonstrated that Camposaurus is definitely a neotheropod

facts.statement: A 2017 phylogenetic analysis found the synonymy with Coelophysis unsupported, placing Camposaurus in a clade with Megapnosaurus, Segisaurus, and Lucianovenator.
facts.quote: The synonymy with Coelophysis was found to be unsupported in 2017 when in a phylogenetic analysis by Ezcurra, Camposaurus was found to be in a clade with Megapnosaurus, Segisaurus, and also Lucianovenator by Martinez & Apaldetti later that year

facts.statement: Camposaurus belongs to the parent group Coelophysinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coelophysinae

facts.statement: Camposaurus is classified in the family Coelophysidae.
facts.quote: Family: Coelophysidae

facts.statement: Camposaurus lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Camposaurus is widely regarded as the oldest known neotheropod dinosaur.
rejected.quote: is widely regarded as the oldest known neotheropod

rejected.quote: Another unique feature is the lack of a large medial condyle on the astragalus
